sources.title: Ernst Hairer, Syvert P. Nørsett, and Gerhard Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations I: Nonstiff Problems, 2nd ed., Chapter III (French excerpt: “Equations Différentielles Ordinaires”)
sources.locator: Chapter III §§III.2–III.5, PDF pp. 4–11 / printed pp. 60–67. Fully rendered and read from the retrieved PDF.
sources.support: §III.2 defines one-step RK updates and local order and derives Euler order one; §III.3 states local-defect and step-Lipschitz hypotheses, then proves the separate global recurrence. The local Euler bound here is independently proved with the stronger componentwise C1 bounds. The global theorem, variable-step controller, and multistep material are not used by this pair.

contents.support: The item states the compact-set convention explicitly and uses the unscaled method-minus-exact defect.

contents.name: Printed p. 62: forward Euler has local order one
contents.support: The source provides context; our proof independently derives the stronger componentwise constant from C1 time/state derivative bounds.

contents.name: Theorem 3.1 and proof, printed pp. 63–65: local defect plus increment stability implies a global error bound
contents.reason: This is the next planned pair’s global propagation theorem; the present pair only defines and proves local defect and one-step stability.

contents.name: Lemma 3.2, printed p. 65: a Lipschitz field gives a Lipschitz Runge–Kutta increment
contents.reason: The statement concerns the stage recursion of Runge–Kutta methods and is used only with their method-specific stage hypotheses.

contents.reason: Variable-step controllers and embedded local-error estimates are assigned to the later adaptive ODE solvers page.

contents.name: Figure III.4, printed p. 63: empirical global error versus numerical work

contents.name: Beginning of §III.5, printed p. 67: multistep-method introduction
contents.reason: Methods using several previous numerical states are assigned to the planned linear multistep page and are not one-step suppliers here.
